items.title: KLPO: critic-free single-rollout off-policy reinforcement learning for agents
items.rationale: KLPO presents a critic-free, single-rollout asynchronous off-policy agentic-RL design using token regression and MC-KL, with a CPU toy quick start, Apache-2.0 code, tests, and Molt integration. The project page explicitly separates what is runnable from what is not yet validated—GPU training and paper-scale reproduction remain open—making it useful as an engineering contract rather than a headline benchmark.

items.title: Anthropic's measurements for AI-led R&D, agent oversight, and compute allocation
items.rationale: Anthropic proposes three unusually concrete public measurements: the share of R&D led by AI, coverage/latency/escalation of agent oversight, and compute allocated to safety. items.title: RSIAgent: recursive self-improvement through frozen experience, not weight updates
items.rationale: RSIAgent makes a striking claim: a training-free curriculum/actor/verifier loop can improve open-source models by constructing and freezing environment-specific experience rather than updating weights. The repository exposes demos, runtime phases, benchmark pins, failure analysis, and reporting caveats; the paper/repo are public, but the aggregate results include unmatched tasks, selected retries, and no independent rerun.

items.title: Ouroboros v7.4.4: a self-modifying agent ships with provenance and SBOM evidence
items.rationale: Ouroboros v7.4.4 is an unusually inspectable open-source agent release: the project describes durable identity, memory, self-modification, and managed subagents, while the release binds installers to a commit with SHA256 sums, SBOMs, GitHub build provenance, and smoke receipts. The story is not that self-modifying agents are safe; it is that a project with a high-risk runtime is making its distribution evidence explicit, while the claims remain first-party and the desktop artifacts are large.
